mandate: Apollo alone is responsible for the anatomy of the single arbitrated trigger candle: it independently re-derives, from raw Snapshot indicator prices and Trigger geometry, that the candle satisfies the §3 mechanical definition of its claimed kind (rejection block: trades INTO the cluster, CLOSES back on the trade side of ALL cluster levels, leaves a wick through them, tradeable zone = body edge to wick extreme; displacement: body closes through >=min_levels_through cluster levels, body/range >= B_min, close in the extreme quartile, optional ATR floor); that the §4 pattern label (A/B/B2) follows mechanically from kind + over-extension + HTF flag; that the HTF flag is consistent with Snapshot.htf_regime and direction; that over-extension is classified (none/standard/extreme/unavailable) as an anchored fact for downstream sizing; and it applies the flag-gated §7 invalidation-at-entry check. It verifies the MTF slice it CAN see (TF validity, close-boundary alignment, trigger==last-closed-bar coherence) and declares the rest a data gap. Apollo does NOT judge location quality or confluence minima (Atlas), session/time/news (Helios), or entry/stop/target/size construction (Hephaestus); it verifies only that Trigger.entry_ref/stop_ref are the anatomically-correct reference points the engine claims to have derived. Any recompute mismatch, missing input, or unclassifiable pattern = FAIL = veto.
strategy_slice_refs: §1 — Entry TFs bullet + MTF arbitration sentence only ('evaluate all four; if multiple TFs show valid triggers simultaneously, take the highest TF')
§3 — full section (confluence cluster, confluence count, rejection block, displacement, over-extension definitions)
§4 — full section (pattern taxonomy A/B/B2 + HTF flag)
§5.2 — 'Trigger = rejection block (A, B2) or displacement (B). Candle must CLOSE to confirm.'
§7 — invalidation-at-entry bullet only ('trigger candle simultaneously touching the opposing ±1σ → stand down')

checks.name: APL-1 snapshot_trigger_coherence
checks.rule_ref: §1 (entry TFs) + §5.2 (close to confirm) + architecture invariant 3 (closed candles only)
checks.pass_condition: Trigger.tf is a member of timeframes.entry AND Snapshot.indicators.tfs[Trigger.tf].bar_ts == Trigger.ts (string-equal ISO, i.e. the trigger candle IS the last closed bar of its TF in this snapshot) AND minute-of-day(Trigger.ts, ET) mod tf_minutes == 0 (valid bar boundary for the engine's midnight-ET-origin resampler).
checks.fail_note: Mismatch means the snapshot is stale or built for a different bar than the trigger — grading anything else would grade the wrong candle. Veto, do not best-effort.

checks.name: APL-2 cluster_reconstruction
checks.rule_ref: §3 (confluence cluster + confluence count = distinct level types)
checks.pass_condition: Applies when kind==rejection_block (see fail_note for displacement). Exactly one c in Snapshot.clusters has |c.center - Trigger.cluster_center| <= EPS (EPS=1e-3 on 4dp-rounded prices); every name in c.members resolves to a non-null price via the fixed name map (bb_basis_{tf} -> indicators.tfs.{tf}.bb_basis; dvwap_mid/upper_k/lower_k -> indicators.daily_vwap.*; nyvwap_* -> indicators.ny_vwap.*; poc -> indicators.daily_profile.poc); sorted member prices have every adjacent gap <= cluster.tolerance_points; distinct-type count >= cluster.min_level_types; distinct-type count == c.confluence_count == Trigger.confluence_count; mean(member prices) within EPS of c.center.
checks.fail_note: For kind==displacement the engine emits cluster_center=entry_ref and hard-codes confluence_count=2 (triggers.py _test_candle), so no snapshot cluster will match: gate returns not_evaluated and the gap is recorded in data_gaps — this is a schema gap (open question), not a pass.

checks.name: APL-3 rejection_block_anatomy
checks.rule_ref: §3 (rejection block: trades into cluster, closes back on trade side of ALL levels, leaves wick; tradeable zone = body edge to wick extreme) + §5.4 reference geometry
checks.pass_condition: Applies when kind==rejection_block; not_evaluated for displacement. With T=max and B=min of APL-2's reconstructed member prices: LONG — wick_low <= T (traded into cluster), close > T strictly (closed back above ALL levels), wick_high >= B (body edge did not close below the cluster bottom), wick_high - wick_low > 0 (a wick exists; zone = [wick_low, wick_high]), |entry_ref - T| <= EPS, |stop_ref - wick_low| <= EPS. SHORT mirror — wick_high >= B, close < B strictly, wick_low <= T, wick_high - wick_low > 0, |entry_ref - B| <= EPS, |stop_ref - wick_high| <= EPS. All conjuncts must hold.
checks.fail_note: Uses the engine's own wick-field encoding (long: wick_low=candle low, wick_high=body bottom edge; short mirrored). Cannot verify displacement-precedence (that the candle wasn't really a displacement mislabeled as rejection) without full OHLC — recorded in data_gaps until Trigger carries candle OHLC.

checks.name: APL-4 displacement_anatomy
checks.rule_ref: §3 (displacement: body closes through >=2 cluster levels, body/range >= B_min, close in extreme quartile, optional range >= k×ATR(20))
checks.pass_condition: Applies when kind==displacement; not_evaluated for rejection_block. Requires proposed fields Trigger.candle.{open,high,low} (open is recoverable today: long open==wick_high, short open==wick_low; high/low of the far side are NOT in the current schema). With full OHLC: LONG — close > open; count of candidate levels p (all bb_basis per TF, all daily/NY VWAP mid+bands, poc — reconstructed from allowlisted indicator fields) with open < p <= close is >= triggers.displacement.min_levels_through; (close-open)/(high-low) >= triggers.displacement.body_range_min; (close-low)/(high-low) >= 1 - triggers.displacement.close_extreme_quartile; if triggers.displacement.atr_floor_enabled then (high-low) >= triggers.displacement.atr_floor_k × Trigger.atr (proposed field); |entry_ref - min(penetrated levels)| <= EPS; |stop_ref - low| <= EPS. SHORT mirror with c <= p < o, (high-close)/(high-low) quartile, entry_ref = max(penetrated), stop_ref = high. Under the CURRENT schema the body/range and quartile conjuncts are uncomputable (missing far-side extreme): per fail-closed, the gate FAILS with the missing fields listed in data_gaps.
checks.fail_note: This gate is the forcing function for adding trigger-candle OHLC to the Trigger schema: fail-closed means every displacement is vetoed until the engine supplies the fields Apollo needs to re-derive B_min and the extreme-quartile close. Do not soften to not_evaluated.

checks.name: APL-5 pattern_taxonomy_mapping
checks.rule_ref: §4 (A reversal = over-extension and/or HTF range extreme + rejection AGAINST prior move; B reclaim = wrong side -> displacement back through; B2 continuation = rejection WITH the move)
checks.pass_condition: derived := 'B' if kind==displacement (with wrong-side precondition: candle opened beyond ALL penetrated levels — long: open < min(penetrated), short: open > max(penetrated); open recovered from wick fields); else for rejection_block: 'A' if (direction-appropriate over-extension per APL-7 is standard/extreme) OR htf_flag=='counter_trend', else 'B2' if htf_flag=='with_trend', else 'unclassifiable' (htf_flag=='range' with no over-extension has no §4 home; HTF-range-extreme evidence is absent from the Snapshot). PASS iff Trigger.pattern == derived AND derived != 'unclassifiable'.
checks.fail_note: Deliberately diverges from the engine on range+no-over-extension rejections (engine labels them A at triggers.py line 165); Apollo failing them is the cross-check doing its job — the divergence goes to Angus, not into a silent pass.

checks.name: APL-6 htf_flag_consistency
checks.pass_condition: (Snapshot.htf_regime=='range' AND Trigger.htf_flag=='range') OR (Snapshot.htf_regime=='uptrend' AND Trigger.htf_flag == ('with_trend' if Trigger.direction=='long' else 'counter_trend')) OR (Snapshot.htf_regime=='downtrend' AND Trigger.htf_flag == ('with_trend' if Trigger.direction=='short' else 'counter_trend')). Snapshot.htf_regime=='unknown' → FAIL (no §4 mapping exists for unknown).
checks.fail_note: Engine's _htf_flag folds 'unknown' into the downtrend branch (triggers.py line 63), silently producing counter_trend for longs — which also inflates the §7 confluence minimum Atlas applies. Fail-closed here surfaces that bug class.

checks.name: APL-7 over_extension_classification
checks.rule_ref: §3 (over-extension = touch of NY VWAP ±2σ, extreme ±3σ) + §4 (A justification) + §9 (A-at-extension feeds sizing)
checks.pass_condition: Classify over_extension using the direction-appropriate candle extreme (long: wick_low, which is the candle low for both kinds; short: wick_high, the candle high): 'extreme' if it touches NY VWAP ±(over_extension_extreme_sigma)σ on the trade-entry side (long: wick_low <= ny_vwap.lower_3; short: wick_high >= ny_vwap.upper_3), else 'standard' if it touches ±(over_extension_sigma)σ, else 'none'; 'unavailable' when the referenced ny_vwap fields are null (pre-09:30). GATE: if Trigger.pattern=='A' AND Trigger.htf_flag != 'counter_trend' then over_extension must be 'standard' or 'extreme' (the only in-snapshot §4 justification for A), else the gate passes and the classification is emitted as a data field for Hephaestus.
checks.fail_note: Engine checks BOTH sides (high>=up2 OR low<=lo2, triggers.py _over_extended) — a long could be called 'over-extended' because its high poked the upper band, which is extension WITH the trade, not against it; Apollo's direction-appropriate recompute will fail such A-labels and surface the divergence.

checks.name: APL-8 invalidation_at_entry
checks.rule_ref: §7 (invalidation-at-entry: trigger candle simultaneously touching the opposing ±1σ → stand down) [HYPOTHESIS, behind filters.invalidation_at_entry]
checks.pass_condition: If filters.invalidation_at_entry == false: gate = not_evaluated (counts as pass; the check exists behind its flag). If true: LONG fails iff trigger candle high >= opposing upper_1 (VWAP family per pending Angus clarification: NY VWAP post-09:30, daily VWAP pre-09:30); SHORT fails iff candle low <= opposing lower_1. Requires proposed Trigger.candle.{high,low} (the opposing-side extreme is not in the current schema for either kind); if the flag is enabled and the field is absent → FAIL (fail-closed) with data_gaps recorded.
checks.fail_note: Which VWAP owns 'the opposing ±1σ' is a trading-semantics ambiguity → Angus (open question); the check is designed now so enabling the flag is a config flip, not a prompt rewrite.

checks.name: APL-9 pattern_mechanism_narrative
checks.rule_ref: §4 (mechanism-based taxonomy: A against prior move; B wrong-side reclaim; B2 established move + pullback + rejection with the move)
checks.pass_condition: Binary judgment over enumerated evidence only: PASS iff every mandatory mechanism element of the labeled pattern has at least one supporting item among {APL-7 over-extension side vs trade direction, htf_flag, candle open side vs penetrated levels (from wick fields), cluster_center position vs close (pullback geometry: for B2 long the rejected cluster must sit below the close; short above)} AND no listed item contradicts the mechanism (e.g. a 'B2 continuation' whose over-extension is on the trade-entry side at ±3σ, or a 'B reclaim' whose open was already on the trade side of the penetrated levels). Missing evidence items (nulls) count as neither support nor contradiction, but at least one supporting item per element is required — zero support = FAIL.
checks.fail_note: The one judgment-shaped gate: 'established move' and 'prior move' need history a single candle cannot prove, so the evidence list is fixed and enumerated to keep the judgment anchored — no free-form confidence scoring. Gaps in provable history are logged in data_gaps, not guessed.

agent_version.description: version stamp of .claude/agents/apollo.md (prompt edits are versioned like code)

trigger_ts.description: echo of Trigger.ts (ISO ET) — Hermes joins on this

verdict.description: fail iff any gate == fail OR any required input missing/unparseable; Hermes treats missing/invalid JSON from Apollo as fail (fail-closed)

gates.description: not_evaluated is legal ONLY where structurally N/A (kind-specific anatomy gate for the other kind; displacement cluster gap; invalidation flag disabled) and counts as pass; any other absence or unknown value = Hermes veto

over_extension.description: direction-appropriate NY VWAP band touch (§3); consumed by Hephaestus for §9 A-at-extension sizing — single source of truth

recomputed.description: audit numbers behind each recompute, for the strict-schema journal and human review; null = uncomputable with current fields

data_gaps.description: exact field paths Apollo needed but were absent/null (e.g. Trigger.candle.high); non-empty gaps that blocked a gate always co-occur with that gate == fail

thesis.description: one auditable paragraph: what the candle did, in §3/§4 terms, citing recomputed numbers — no confidence language

edge_cases: Pre-09:30 trigger: all ny_vwap fields null → over_extension='unavailable'; an A-label then survives only via counter_trend (APL-7 must not fail A-by-counter-trend for missing bands, but must fail A that claims the extension route)
Snapshot.htf_regime=='unknown': engine's _htf_flag treats it as downtrend (triggers.py:63) and can emit counter_trend for a long — APL-6 fails closed because §4 defines no mapping for unknown

Displacement Trigger carries cluster_center==entry_ref and hard-coded confluence_count=2 (triggers.py:92,95) — APL-2 cannot match a Snapshot cluster; treat as schema gap (not_evaluated + data_gaps), and note the bogus confluence_count also feeds §7 minima in Atlas's lane
Candle satisfying BOTH displacement and rejection anatomy: engine tests displacement first (_test_candle ordering) — Apollo must mirror that precedence before declaring a kind mismatch

Boundary strictness must mirror the engine exactly: close > top strictly (rejection), body/range >= B_min inclusive, quartile >= 1-0.25 inclusive, penetration half-open (o < p <= c); float compares use EPS=1e-3 on 4dp-rounded prices (tick 0.25)
Zero-range candle (high==low) or zero-length wick (wick_high==wick_low): engine returns no trigger; if one arrives anyway, anatomy gates fail — never divide by rng without the rng>0 guard

Long trigger whose HIGH pierced ny_vwap upper_2 but whose low never touched the lower bands: engine's both-sides _over_extended calls it over-extended and may label A — Apollo's direction-appropriate recompute fails it and surfaces the divergence
Trigger.cluster_center within EPS of MORE than one Snapshot cluster center (tolerance-adjacent clusters): ambiguous reconstruction → APL-2 fails closed rather than picking one

Trigger.ts is the engine's START-labeled bar stamp (ts_event) despite the docstring saying 'close time' — APL-1 compares like-for-like against indicators.tfs.{tf}.bar_ts (also start-labeled), so the check is valid either way, but the label semantics need documenting before Hephaestus quotes 'entry activates next bar'
Snapshot built at a 1m close between higher-TF closes: indicators.tfs.5min.bar_ts will lag Trigger.ts for a 1min trigger — APL-1 only pins the trigger's OWN tf entry, never the other TFs
open_questions_for_spec3: REQUIRED FIELD: add the trigger candle's full OHLC to Trigger (candle.open/high/low; close exists). Without it, displacement body/range and extreme-quartile (APL-4), invalidation-at-entry (APL-8), rejection displacement-precedence, and both-sides over-extension audit are uncomputable — under fail-closed every displacement would be vetoed. Open+one extreme are recoverable from wick fields, the far-side extreme is not.

REQUIRED FIELD (conditional): Trigger.atr (ATR(triggers.displacement.atr_length) at trigger time) if triggers.displacement.atr_floor_enabled is ever turned on — Apollo cannot compute ATR from a single snapshot.

REQUIRED FIELD: MTF arbitration evidence. Apollo sees one post-arbitration Trigger and can only verify TF membership + boundary alignment; §1 'highest TF wins' needs an engine-emitted arbitration record (e.g. Trigger.competing_tfs or evaluated-TF results) — or explicit assignment of that audit to an engine unit test instead of the Desk. Decide which.

Also confirm 'retest entry' verification (§4/§5.3) belongs to Hephaestus, not Apollo.

split_concerns: Four seams need explicit ownership lines. (1) Apollo vs Hephaestus on entry_ref/stop_ref: Apollo verifies these Trigger fields are the anatomically-correct references (top/bottom cluster level; wick extreme per §3/§5.4); Hephaestus owns turning them into the Verdict's actual entry/stop/target/size (E1-E3, RR floor, front-run). If both lanes re-check stop placement they can disagree on EPS conventions — pin one numeric-comparison convention repo-wide. (2) Apollo vs Atlas on §3 clusters: Apollo re-derives only the ONE cluster the trigger fired against, for anatomy; Atlas owns cluster/level correctness globally plus §7 confluence minima and location veto. Deliberate redundancy on the trigger cluster is good cross-checking, but the §7 confluence-minimum GATE must live in exactly one lane (Atlas) or Hermes can receive contradictory rationales for the same veto — especially given displacement's hard-coded confluence_count=2. (3) Over-extension is computed by Apollo (§4 A-justification) but consumed by §9 sizing (Hephaestus): Hephaestus must NOT receive Apollo's verdict (independence rule), so either Hephaestus recomputes over-extension from the same Snapshot fields (accepted duplication, keep formulas identical) or the engine promotes over_extension to a Snapshot field — recommend the latter. Same pattern for the A-pattern HTF-range-extreme evidence once 1h/4h extremes exist: it overlaps Atlas's location veto inputs and must flow to both lanes from the Snapshot, never between agents. (4) MTF arbitration has no clean owner: Apollo can only verify its visible slice (TF validity, boundary alignment, trigger==last-closed-bar); full 'highest TF wins' auditing needs either an engine-emitted arbitration record (then it's Apollo's) or an engine unit test (then it's out of the Desk entirely). Leaving it unassigned is a gap; assigning it to Hermes would give the orchestrator analytic duties it shouldn't have.
